notes: Independent review of issue #1243's extraction (cc-39fac3); cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files. All nine routes accepted and all fifteen findings confirmed; nothing corrected in place and nothing added. Provenance: the recorded sha256 of the Springer open-access PDF matches byte for byte, and the paper is 120 pages, confirmed three independent ways (linearization /N, a page-tree /Count, and 120 /Type /Page objects). **Version discipline matters here and the extraction got it right.** arXiv:2006.13647's e-print is a single gzipped file dated May 2020 — a year before the paper was even received — and is not the accepted version: its appendix section headers are all commented out, so the appendix carrying E13 and E14 does not exist there as a numbered appendix. Comparing numbering, five of the eight cited statements agree between versions and three do not: 5.14 is a Theorem in print and a Corollary in the 2020 draft, and A.1 and A.3 have no counterpart. All eight are correct in the published text the extraction says it read. A practical note for whoever checks this paper next: the article is pp. 171-290 of the volume in a 120-page PDF, so printed page n is PDF page n - 170. The status split — 39 planned against 21 missing and 1 library — is the most distinctive thing about this extraction and it is justified: each planned item quotes the atlas stage that already plans it, and for the paper's main theorem that stage, AutomorphicCongruences:L3, names Nakamura's universal zeta morphism explicitly. This is the rare extraction whose principal job was to recognise that the work was already planned rather than to plan it again. The single library item cites mathlib:PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassFactorization and mathlib:PowerSeries.IsWeierstrassFactorization.unique for the definition of mu and lambda at §5.1; both exist in Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean and the citation is apt. One reservation worth recording rather than acting on: `baseline` is null, so no pinned commits are recorded at all — the thinnest library record I have met in this corpus, even though the two declarations check out.
